articles.title: Flor do 'cheiro de cemitério' ganha versão para decorar até casamentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Crisântemo, tradicionalmente associado a cemitérios, perdeu o perfume característico após cruzamento genético e passou a ser usado em casamentos, festas de 15 anos e outras celebrações.
articles.summary: Crisântemo, tradicionalmente associado a cemitérios, perdeu o perfume característico após cruzamento genético e passou a ser usado em casamentos, festas de 15 anos e outras celebra
articles.body:
Tradicionalmente associada a cemitérios e cerimônias fúnebres, uma flor está ganhando espaço em um cenário bem diferente: a decoração de casamentos, festas de 15 anos, aniversários e bodas.

Para isso, o crisântemo passou por um processo de melhoramento genético que suavizou o perfume característico da espécie , uma mudança que ajudou a aumentar a procura pela variedade comercializada por uma produtora do interior de São Paulo.

A novidade foi apresentada durante a 32ª edição do Veiling Market, principal feira de negócios de flores e plantas ornamentais do Brasil realizada na Cooperativa Veiling Holambra , em Santo Antônio de Posse (SP).

Entre as tendências da feira, também estava o uso de plantas que podem contribuir para a remoção ou retenção de determinados compostos presentes no ar de ambientes internos.

No caso do crisântemo, a mudança no cheiro foi acompanhada por uma transformação no uso da flor. A empresa que produz e comercializa a variedade sem o perfume característico afirma que atualmente cerca de 80% de sua produção é formada por essa opção .

Segundo Ana Carolina Pinotti, da área comercial da empresa, a produção também cresceu com o aumento da demanda. Em 2024, eram produzidos cerca de 10 mil vasos por semana. Atualmente, são 36 mil.

O crescimento, no entanto, é um dado específico da produtora e não significa que as vendas de crisântemos tenham aumentado na mesma proporção em todo o mercado.

Com melhoramento genético e odor mais suave, crisântemos deixam de ser usados apenas em cerimônias fúnebres e decora até casamentos — Foto: Karina Saab

A associação do crisântemo com cemitérios é um dos fatores que historicamente dificultaram sua utilização em determinados tipos de decoração. A mudança genética buscou justamente alterar uma característica que contribuía para essa percepção.

Maritha Domhof, sócia-proprietária da Flores Rancho Raízes, explica que a empresa trabalhou com geneticistas para chegar à nova variedade.

“Tinha um grande preconceito e, por isso, foi trabalhado com os geneticistas. Eles alteraram o cruzamento do crisântemo e, com isso, conseguiram alterar esse detalhe", explicou.

Segundo Maritha, a nova variedade não é completamente sem odor . O que mudou foi o perfume característico do crisântemo tradicional, que agora passa a ter um cheiro mais sutil.

Além da mudança no aroma, existem variedades com pétalas de duas cores .

A empresa afirma que a combinação de cores, formatos e tamanhos também ajuda a ampliar as possibilidades de uso da flor.

A procura para eventos cresceu, segundo a produtora. A flor, que antes não era vendida pela empresa para esse tipo de finalidade, passou a ser utilizada em diferentes celebrações.

“É usado muito em casamentos, festa de 15 anos, aniversários e grandes festas de bodas. Por exemplo, bodas de prata, bodas de ouro. Então, eles fazem toda a decoração e eles têm a grande opção de ter muitas e muitas cores”, diz Maritha.

A mudança não significou aumento no preço provocado pelo melhoramento genético. De acordo com Maritha, o valor continuou seguindo o mercado , enquanto as mudas foram alteradas geneticamente.

A variedade comercializada pela empresa tem genética desenvolvida por um breeder — termo usado para profissionais ou empresas responsáveis pelo desenvolvimento de novas variedades na Holanda.

E esse melhoramento genético de plantas busca combinar características desejadas de diferentes variedades.

Segundo Lídia Soarte, que também trabalha na produção de flores, o processo reproduz de forma controlada um mecanismo que também acontece naturalmente com a participação de agentes como abelhas e pássaros.

“Esse melhoramento genético são empresas que fazem, elas tentam fazer o cruzamento de plantas que têm alguma característica boa com uma outra planta que tem uma outra característica para melhorar a planta”, explicou.

Crisântemos: combinação de cores, formatos e tamanhos também ajuda a ampliar as possibilidades de uso da flor — Foto: Bianca Garutti

O desenvolvimento de uma nova variedade não termina no cruzamento. Conforme Lídia, o trabalho pode levar cerca de cinco anos antes de a planta chegar aos produtores interessados .

Depois disso, são realizados testes para verificar características como durabilidade, produção, coloração e adaptação ao clima.

“A partir daí que vai até os produtores que têm interesse nessas variedades, que fazem o teste na própria produção para ver se realmente produzindo tem toda a durabilidade de boa produção, a cor realmente, porque às vezes diferencia de clima a cor que acaba vindo”, disse Lídia.

De acordo com Lídia, muitos dos melhoristas de variedades estão em países europeus, como Alemanha, Dinamarca, Holanda e França.

Depois de chegar ao Brasil, a planta passa por testes para verificar sua adaptação às condições locais e a aceitação dos consumidores.

Plantas capazes de deixar o 'ar mais puro'

Além da novidade com os crisântemos, a feira também apresentou o projeto “Plante Ar Puro”, que reúne espécies associadas à melhoria da qualidade do ar em ambientes internos .

Segundo a organização do Veiling Market, a iniciativa é inspirada em estudos realizados pela Nasa sobre o uso de plantas em espaços fechados e os efeitos sobre determinados compostos presentes no ar.

De acordo com Denis Martins, analista de produtos da cooperativa, algumas espécies são estudadas pela capacidade de absorver substâncias que podem estar presentes em ambientes internos, como compostos liberados por tintas, produtos de limpeza e outros materiais.

🪴 Elas podem ser cultivadas dentro de casa e, além da função ornamental, são apresentadas como opções que podem contribuir para ambientes mais agradáveis .

Durante o evento, a proposta foi levada para uma bolha inflável transparente, onde os visitantes podiam entrar e permanecer por alguns minutos cercados pelas plantas.

A experiência foi criada para transmitir a sensação de estar em um ambiente com ar mais limpo e renovado.

"O ar lá é diferente, a gente sente um ar mais puro, mais renovado”, comentou a agrônoma Liane Kazuko Yamamoto Fukuda, de São Paulo.

Principal feira de negócios de flores e plantas ornamentais do Brasil reforçou uso de espécies associadas à melhoria da qualidade do ar em ambientes internos — Foto: Bianca Garutti

A resposta que o projeto tenta mostrar é que sim. Não é preciso ter uma estrutura como a montada na feira. Os vasos podem ser distribuídos de acordo com o tamanho, a luminosidade e as características de cada ambiente.

Segundo Thamara D’Angieri, gerente de Marketing e Produto da Cooperativa Veiling Holambra, qualquer ambiente pode receber algumas dessas espécies. A quantidade, porém, depende do tamanho do espaço e do porte das plantas .

Segundo a gerente, em ambientes menores, plantas de porte compacto podem ser uma alternativa. Para locais maiores, espécies mais volumosas, como a samambaia, podem ser distribuídas em maior quantidade.

Thamara explica que a escolha também pode levar em consideração o quanto cada planta exige de cuidados.

A espada-de-são-jorge, por exemplo, é conhecida pela resistência e pela facilidade de cultivo.

Para quem prefere flores, há opções como antúrio, lírio-da-paz e azaleia.

articles.standfirst: Pesquisadores explicam que o cérebro cria vínculos reais com personagens e pode reagir ao fim de histórias com sensação de vazio e até uma espécie de luto.
articles.summary: Pesquisadores explicam que o cérebro cria vínculos reais com personagens e pode reagir ao fim de histórias com sensação de vazio e até uma espécie de luto.
articles.body:
Já faz anos que pesquisadores estudam o que chamam de "depressão pós-série". Não é a depressão clínica propriamente falando, mas a sensação de vazio que surge quando uma série que a gente passou bastante tempo assintindo simplesmente chega ao fim.

Isso ocorre porque nosso cérebro forma uma conexão real com os personagens. Afinal, o circuito neural que ele usa para se apegar a esses personagens é o mesmo que se aplica a pessoas da vida real. É assim que nascem as chamadas "relações parassociais".

Um nome chique para aquela mesma sensação que a gente tem de que determinados artistas ou criadores de conteúdo são como nossos amigos pessoais.

E quando chega a hora de dizer adeus à série em questão, nosso cérebro acha que está lidando com um término ou uma morte e entra numa espécie de luto.

Quem nunca ficou travado na fase de negação reassistindo à série inteira de cabo a rabo infinitas vezes? E isso não é exclusivo das séries. Também é possível sentir esse luto pelo fim de livros, carreiras e até mesmo games.

É o que revelou recentemente este estudo que batizou o processo de "depressão pós-jogo". Um sentimento que pode se tornar tão intenso a ponto de a pessoa ficar com medo de começar um novo jogo. É como quando alguém termina um relacionamento e precisa tomar coragem para voltar para a vida de solteiro.

articles.title: Corpos de 30 vítimas de incêndio em balsa nas Filipinas chegam a porto para identificação | G1
articles.standfirst: Incêndio no MV June Aster matou ao menos 35 pessoas e deixou mais de 50 desaparecidas. Buscas continuam dentro da embarcação.
articles.summary: Incêndio no MV June Aster matou ao menos 35 pessoas e deixou mais de 50 desaparecidas. Buscas continuam dentro da embarcação.
articles.body:
Os corpos de 30 vítimas do incêndio em uma balsa nas Filipinas chegaram neste sábado (12) ao porto de Borac, na província de Palawan, para identificação. As vítimas foram encontradas carbonizadas dentro da embarcação.

O incêndio no MV June Aster, ocorrido na noite de quarta-feira (9), deixou ao menos 35 mortos e mais de 50 desaparecidos. Segundo a Guarda Costeira filipina, 43 pessoas sobreviveram.

Equipes de resgate transferem os restos mortais das vítimas do recente incêndio na balsa MV June Aster — Foto: PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD via AP

Os corpos foram levados da balsa até o porto por outra embarcação e entregues à Unidade Forense Provincial. Tendas foram montadas no local para receber as vítimas e auxiliar no trabalho das autoridades.

As buscas continuam porque ainda há corpos dentro do MV June Aster, segundo a Guarda Costeira. As autoridades não informaram quantos.

A balsa havia partido de Manila e estava perto da vila de Turda, a cerca de 39 quilômetros de Coron, seu destino, quando o incêndio começou.

GIF Balsa em chamas nas Filipinas — Foto: Reuters

A causa do fogo ainda não foi determinada. Um dos sobreviventes relatou ter ouvido uma explosão e afirmou que o incêndio pode ter começado no porão de carga. Segundo as autoridades, as chamas e a fumaça se espalharam rapidamente, impulsionadas pelo vento.

Sobreviventes também relataram que tudo aconteceu em poucos minutos, sem tempo para pegar os coletes salva-vidas.

Arnulfo Nokki Villanueva, um dos passageiros resgatados, disse a um veículo de imprensa local que tentou buscar um colete, mas não conseguiu por causa do pânico dentro da embarcação.

A Guarda Costeira investiga ainda se uma lona colocada para proteger áreas abertas da chuva pode ter dificultado a saída dos passageiros.

Os investigadores devem verificar se os procedimentos de emergência foram seguidos, incluindo o acionamento do alarme, as orientações dadas aos passageiros e a assistência prestada pela tripulação.

A Guarda Costeira também procura o capitão da balsa. Segundo relatos recebidos pelas autoridades, ele teria sobrevivido, mas seu nome não aparece na lista oficial de sobreviventes.

Investigações marítima e criminal vão analisar as circunstâncias do incêndio e uma eventual responsabilidade do capitão e dos demais tripulantes.

Imagens divulgadas pela Guarda Costeira mostram o interior da embarcação destruído pelo fogo, com estruturas metálicas e veículos carbonizados.

Familiares dos desaparecidos aguardam a identificação dos corpos. Lira Daco, cuja filha de 20 anos está desaparecida, afirmou estar angustiada com a possibilidade de a jovem estar entre as vítimas encontradas dentro do navio.

O manifesto da balsa registrava inicialmente 134 pessoas, sendo 117 passageiros e 17 tripulantes. Dois passageiros listados informaram posteriormente que não haviam embarcado. Assim, 132 pessoas estavam efetivamente a bordo, segundo a Guarda Costeira.

A embarcação, de 53 metros, tinha capacidade para transportar 306 passageiros e 27 tripulantes.

Dois turistas chilenos estão entre os sobreviventes. Eles já deixaram Coron, e as autoridades filipinas mantêm contato com a embaixada do Chile.

A Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc., proprietária da balsa, afirmou que presta assistência aos passageiros e familiares e coopera com as autoridades nas buscas pelos desaparecidos e na investigação sobre a causa do incêndio.

articles.title: SC's 13 queries to FSSAI: 'Give details on shape, size, colour of food label'
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has directed FSSAI to spell out details of how front-of-pack food warning labels will look, their shape, size, colour, placem.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has directed FSSAI to spell out details of how front-of-pack food warning labels will look, their shape, size, colour, placement on packets and the timeline of implementation, leaving nothing to the discretion of the food regulator.The court also wanted to know how Centre plans to warn children about the dangers of junk food.After FSSAI agreed to implement labelling after being pushed by SC and filed an affidavit, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran put 13 questions to the regulator and gave 10 days' time for answers.Though SC acknowledged "significant progress" has been made by FSSAI on this issue of national importance, it said the regulator's affidavit was silent on various issues and several aspects of practical implementation required clarification.The 13 questions are part of the detailed order uploaded by the court on Friday, which also includes its observations from the previous day on why FSSAI proposed a two-phase rollout of the labelling requirements instead of implementing them in one go.'Red hexagon' to send out warning to customersAccording to FSSAI’s proposal, during Phase I, a red hexagonal warning would be placed on products high in two or more nutrients of concern, namely added fat, added sugar and salt, based on thresholds in the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024. The warning could carry declarations such as “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR”, “HIGH SALT” and “HIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGE”. The proposed Phase II would extend the warning to products high in any one of the specified nutrients. The order questions the regulator on what basis it suggested the inclusion of food products high in “two or more” nutrients of concern and certain sweetened beverages in Phase I, and the inclusion of food products high in “any one” nutrient of concern in Phase II, respectively.The court also said sugar, salt and fat are called the “Unholy Trinity” and that “the ‘unholiness’ arises not only from the added sugar and added fat in a food product but the total value of these nutrients available in a product, which has to be considered.” The Supreme Court incorporated the suggestion of advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi that the threshold must be decided based on “total sugar” and “total fat” and not on the basis of “added sugar” and “added fat”. Referring to the 2021 FSSAI meeting, the Bench said, “It is clear from the aforesaid minutes that ‘total sugar’ and ‘saturated fat’ would be used for the purpose of the labelling. In this regard, we would like FSSAI to weigh in and indicate whether there has been a change in stance in comparison to the consensus arrived at in the aforesaid stakeholder consultation. If so, we would like to know how the underlying concerns are sought to be addressed.”The court also asked the regulator: “What are the dimensions of the ‘red hexagon’ proposed to be used in the FoPL (labelling)? Whether it would have standardised specifications or whether it would be calculated in proportion to the area of the package? Whether the font size used for FoPL would be relative to the dimensions of the hexagon themselves? The manner and method of the placement of such hexagon(s)?” It further asked, “Why has FSSAI suggested a combined/composite/singular hexagon for two or more nutrients of concern instead of separate/distinct/individual hexagons for each nutrient of concern?” The court posted the matter for hearing on September 28.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Middle East News: On the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11 attacks, al-Qaida's official media wing, As-Sahab, has released a propaganda video featuring the first-ever foo.
articles.body: On the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11 attacks, al-Qaida's official media wing, As-Sahab, has released a propaganda video featuring the first-ever footage of Hamza bin Laden, the son and designated heir of Osama bin Laden. The video's release has drawn scrutiny from intelligence analysts, primarily because Hamza was reported to have been killed in a US counterterrorism operation along the Afghan-Pakistan border around 2019.The 50-minute-long video titled "A Quarter Century of the 11 September Raids" also features unseen images of slain AQ chief Ayman Al Zawahiri. The outfit has not acknowledged his death to date or issued its customary funeral eulogy. The video aims to propagate the ideological doctrine associated with the current outfit chief, Saif al-Adl, with the Bin Laden name aimed at recruitment.Intriguingly, the video opens not with international operations, but with historical footage from the Sept 2014 al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent attack on the Karachi naval dockyard. Intelligence sources noted that prioritising this regional operation underscores the influence of Pakistani terrorists within both al-Qaida's central leadership and its propaganda apparatus.Visually, the footage, they said, was meticulously staged to evoke a sense of ideological nostalgia. Hamza appears multiple times in the footage, seated against a stark, cracked mud wall, clad in a traditional white turban with an assault rifle propped beside him. "The deliberate choice of staging serves a clear dual purpose: establishing Hamza's authority as his father's successor while invoking the classic visual identity of early global jihadism," said a source.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: HYDERABAD: A retired havildar who had been fired from his post-retirement job in June by the Army for indiscipline, single-handedly stole 12 military grade weapons and ammunition from the Madras Regiment armoury at Bollarum on Aug 30 night. Officers said he carried the guns out of the heavily guarded cantonment on his Activa scooter.Senior police officers said on Friday that the ex-serviceman, 37-year-old Upputholla Mallesh, who was upset with his superiors after being fired, is believed to have stolen the weapons, including five assault rifles and seven pistols, as a form of revenge. However, investigators said the real motive still needs to be probed.Investigators said the case was cracked after Mallesh’s wife and father-in-law were questioned by the investigators. The wife later confronted the accused about the theft and forced him to surrender before the authorities. Mallesh also helped the police recover the weapons. TOI was the first to report on Friday morning that the case had been solved and the weapons recovered.Speaking to reporters, DGP C V Anand said Mallesh had been arrested and the weapons recovered from an open field in Nagarkurnool district from under stacks of hay, about 185 km from Bollarum.The accused, who previously worked in the 20th battalion of the Madras Regiment had planned the theft meticulously and even conducted a recce of the armoury for two days, on Aug 28 and 29. articles.title: China Southern to resume Guangzhou-Delhi flights after 6 years ahead of Xi's Brics visit
articles.summary: India News: China Southern Airlines will restart regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from September 21, the Global Times reported on Saturda.
articles.body: China Southern Airlines will restart regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from September 21, the Global Times reported on Saturday.The announcement came ahead of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s visit to India for the Brics summit. The airline said the resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in South Asia to more than 100 flights a week. The Guangzhou-New Delhi service had been suspended for six years.Direct air links between India and China returnAir connectivity between India and China has gradually improved in recent months.Air China resumed its Beijing-Delhi service in April, while China Eastern Airlines restarted direct flights between Kunming and Kolkata on April 18.Indian carrier IndiGo also launched a daily non-stop service between Kolkata and Shanghai on March 30. The airline had earlier restored flights from Kolkata to Guangzhou and later began operating from Delhi to the Chinese city.The resumption of direct flights followed confirmation from India’s ministry of external affairs. Air links between the two countries had been suspended during the Covid-19 pandemic and amid tensions following the Doklam and Galwan standoffs.Xi leaves for Brics summitXi left Beijing on Saturday for the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi at Modi’s invitation, China’s state news agency Xinhua reported.The Chinese president is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later in the day.Xi’s delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China and director of its General Office, and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.According to Xinhua, Xi is expected to advance proposals on cooperation among Global South countries, building on his remarks at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.Brics has become a major platform for emerging economies to coordinate on trade, finance, technology, development and global governance. articles.title: Gujarat’s new Panchayat Tax rule: Relief for soldiers, veterans and war widows
articles.summary: News News: Gujarat has amended its rules to exempt residential houses owned or occupied by serving defence personnel, their spouses, former soldiers and widows o.
articles.body: Gujarat has amended its rules to exempt residential houses owned or occupied by serving defence personnel, their spouses, former soldiers and widows of soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice from Panchayat Tax. The decision applies to eligible beneficiaries whose residential property falls within the limits of a Gram Panchayat in Gujarat, with the exemption restricted to one residential house.The measure is intended to reduce the tax burden on the residential homes of soldiers and their families and provide them with direct financial relief. It also described the move as an expression of respect for the service of defence personnel and the sacrifices made by soldiers.Widows of soldiers included in tax reliefA specific provision has been made for widows of soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice. The government said extending the exemption to their residential homes reflects its sensitivity towards and respect for their sacrifice.The provision covers the homes of families of soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation, with the government saying the exemption is a way of expressing gratitude to these families.The benefit, however, is not a blanket exemption on residential properties. It is limited to a single residential house used by an eligible beneficiary.Amendment follows draft rules issued in 2025The final decision comes after the government first proposed changes to the existing rules. Draft rules amending the ‘Gujarat Gram and Nagar Panchayats Taxes and Fees Rules, 1964’ were published in the Extraordinary Gazette of the Government of Gujarat in December 2025.The draft invited objections and suggestions from concerned persons. The government said it considered the objections and suggestions received before issuing the final amended rules.The State Government has now notified the Gujarat Gram and Nagar Panchayats Taxes and Fees (Amendment) Rules, 2026, using the powers conferred on it under the Gujarat Panchayats Act, 1993.The amended rules will take effect from the date they are published in the Official Gazette.The government said exempting the homes of serving soldiers, veterans and widows of soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice is a step towards their welfare and that of their families. articles.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
articles.summary: The East-West pipeline has helped the country - the world's largest crude oil exporter - bypass closures in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia has closed a critical oil pipeline after it was attacked by drones launched from Iraq, as conflict in the Middle East widens.

Iraq said it had fired a military commander and launched an investigation after admitting the drone attack on its neighbour's East-West pipeline had originated in one of its provinces bordering Iran.

The 1,200km (745 mile) pipeline has helped Saudi Arabia - the world's largest crude oil exporter - bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The incident comes amid a major advance by the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, putting more pressure on global oil shipping routes as the US-Iran war stretches into its seventh month.

Riyadh on Friday said it had shut the pipeline as a precaution, as satellite images of scorched ground and smoke near the site emerged.

The foreign ministry said the attack resulted in some injuries and damage, which was still being assessed.

The pipeline has been moving 4% to 5% of global oil supply, news agency Reuters has reported, citing ship tracking companies and analysts.

Saudi Arabia has chosen not to retaliate at this stage, its foreign ministry says, following a call from Iraq's prime minister.

It said the kingdom would "support the efforts of the Iraqi government" to "prevent attacks" launched from the country against neighbouring states.

"The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia affirms that it reserves its right to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and security, protect its facilities, and ensure the safety of its citizens and residents," the statement added.

The Iraqi prime minister's office in its own statement said the operations commander in the Maysan governorate - a province which borders Iran - had been removed from his post following confirmation the drone attack had been launched from that region.

How Houthi gains in Yemen could drive up oil prices

The Gulf Co-operation Council – made up of representatives from the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait – also issued a missive condemning the attack.

"This attack represents a dangerous escalation and an unacceptable threat to the security of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its territorial integrity, and its vital installations, as well as a flagrant violation of the principles of international law," secretary general Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi.

This week, a lightning advance in Yemen has also seen Houthi militants seize control of much of the country's coastline , sources say.

The group claims it has control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, though it says maritime navigation is "safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels".

The developments have squeezed both sides of the Arabian Peninsula, pushing crude oil prices to over $100 a barrel for the first time since July .

articles.summary: India News: Chinese president Xi Jinping landed in New Delhi for the 18th Brics summit, where he will hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and present Bei.
articles.body: Chinese president Xi Jinping landed in New Delhi for the 18th Brics summit, where he will hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and present Beijing’s proposals for greater cooperation among Global South countries.Ahead of the meeting, China’s state-run Global Times described Brics as an increasingly important platform at a time of global uncertainty. In an editorial, the Chinese government mouthpiece said the grouping’s strength came from its commitment to openness, cooperation and fairness."The key lies in its commitment to openness and inclusiveness, its goal of win-win cooperation and its pursuit of fairness and justice. The more turbulent and transformative the world becomes, the more the unique value of Brics cooperation comes into focus. As greater Brics cooperation enters a stage of improving quality and efficiency, there is growing confidence that Brics cooperation has enormous potential and that the future of Brics countries is bright."Xi expected to outline China’s prioritiesXi is expected to exchange views with other leaders on the international situation, the future development of Brics and ways to deepen practical cooperation. The newspaper said Xi would also put forward China’s initiatives for expanding and improving cooperation within the grouping."Since 2013, President Xi has put forward a series of important proposals and initiatives, including the "Brics Plus" cooperation model, driving the rapid development of Brics cooperation and enabling it to deliver greater results, while playing a pivotal role at every critical juncture in the mechanism's development."The editorial also highlighted China’s support for the New Development Bank, the expansion of Brics and cooperation in areas such as peace, innovation, green development and people-to-people exchanges."From advocating the Brics Spirit of "openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation" to proposing the concept of the "Brics Plus" cooperation model; from championing the establishment of the New Development Bank in Shanghai to supporting the historic expansion of Brics and proposing to build a Brics committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges, China has actively worked to strengthen and expand Brics cooperation, continuously improved the mechanism in line with changing times and steadily enhanced its global influence, earning broad recognition from all sides," the editorial adds.China to lead Brics in 2027China will take over the rotating Brics presidency in 2027. The Global Times said Beijing would use the term to strengthen unity through multilateralism and align development strategies among member countries.It said China would also promote its Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative. The newspaper identified the digital economy, green development, artificial intelligence, poverty reduction and agriculture as areas where China would seek concrete outcomes.The editorial concluded, "A 'Greater Brics' that is more united, efficient, pragmatic and committed to shouldering its responsibilities will surely open up new space for the common development of the Global South and inject greater certainty and positive energy into a world beset by turbulence and change."India is hosting the 18th Brics summit under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held separate bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in New Delhi on Saturday, with India seeking to deepen cooperation with both countries in defence, investment and emerging sectors.Sources said the talks with Ethiopia and Malaysia marked a new trajectory in India's relations with the two countries. Ethiopia, in particular, expressed interest in Indian mining companies, while discussions with Malaysia covered opportunities in the semiconductor sector, according to the sources.PM Modi met Anwar on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, where Malaysia is participating as a BRICS partner country at India's invitation. The Malaysian prime minister is scheduled to deliver a national statement on "Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth" at the summit.According to Malaysia's Foreign Ministry, the country is expected to push for stronger cooperation among BRICS members and partner countries on development challenges, economic opportunities and ensuring more inclusive access to technological advances and innovation.Anwar is also scheduled to visit Kerala, with the visit aimed at strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in areas including trade and investment, the digital economy, talent and labour, education and regional connectivity.PM Modi also met Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed at Hyderabad House. Ethiopia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2024, alongside Egypt, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.The latest talks build on growing India-Ethiopia defence engagement. Earlier this month, officials from the two countries discussed ways to expand cooperation in military training, defence industry collaboration and UN peacekeeping. The discussions also covered new and emerging areas of defence cooperation.The ministry of defence had said after the meeting between Ethiopian Charge d'Affaires Nebiyu Tedla and Defence Ministry Joint Secretary Amitabh Prasad that the two sides discussed "avenues to further strengthen India-Ethiopia defence cooperation, including training, defence industry collaboration and UN Peacekeeping, with focus on new and emerging areas."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: European expat who moved to India for work shares an unexpected behavior pattern in most Indians when they introduce themselves: ‘People want to place you…’

articles.body: Moving to a new country for work often means adjusting to a different routine, food, language and way of doing things. For one European expat who moved to India, however, one of the more unexpected differences emerged not at work or while navigating daily life, but during conversations with people he had just met.The experience was shared online and has since drawn attention to a particular aspect of social interactions in India.The European expat spoke about his experience after moving to India for work, describing something he found striking about the way people introduce themselves and present their background.‘People want to place you in a social hierarchy’In the account shared on the r/india subreddit, the expat said he noticed that conversations could quickly move beyond the usual introductions. Rather than simply talking about themselves, some people would mention details about their education, profession, family background or other markers of status.What stood out to him was the sense that these details were being used to understand where a person stood socially. The expat described the experience as people wanting to “place you in a social hierarchy”.The comment has prompted reactions online, with some people saying they recognised the behaviour he was describing, while others pointed out that introductions and social interactions can vary considerably depending on the setting, city and people involved.The post sparked different reactionsThe response online was not entirely one-sided. Some users agreed with the expat's observation and said that people in India can sometimes be quick to establish someone's social or professional standing.Others suggested that this behaviour should not be treated as universal. The way people introduce themselves can differ between workplaces, friend groups, cities and generations.The discussion also reflects one of the less obvious parts of moving abroad: cultural differences are not always found in major traditions or everyday practicalities. Sometimes, they appear in small interactions that people in the host country may consider completely ordinary.For the European expat, it was one such interaction that became an unexpected culture shock after moving to India.Why introductions can carry more informationIn many Indian conversations, a person's introduction may include details that go beyond their name and profession. Questions about where someone studied, where they work, where their family is from or what their parents do can sometimes become part of an early conversation.For someone unfamiliar with these social cues, the amount of information exchanged can feel unusual.That appears to have been the expat's larger observation: that introductions were not always just about getting to know an individual, but could also provide clues about their social and professional background.His experience has since become part of a wider online conversation about the differences foreigners notice after moving to India.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: In 1978, Apple was destroying its first computers; Steve Jobs sent a letter to an engineer, with $400, asking to return the machine; he declined; 50 years later it may get $800,000 in auction

articles.body: Apple spent much of 1977 and 1978 trying to make its first computer disappear. In January 1978, the company’s co-founder Steve Jobs wrote to New Orleans engineer Fred Hatfield, offering him $400 and an upgraded board in exchange for his Apple-1, with instructions to send the old machine back so it could be destroyed. Hatfield declined. Nearly 50 years later, that decision has turned his Apple-1 into an auction lot with an estimate of up to $800,000.The Hatfield Apple-1 will be sold as part of Bonhams' History of Science, Technology & Computing sale, which will run online from October 4 through October 14, with an estimate of $500,000 to $800,000. It is one of fewer than 75 verified Apple-1 computers known to survive and remains listed as operational.Steve Wozniak's signature and Steve Jobs’ letter that outlasted Apple's own plans for the machineThe motherboard carries Steve Wozniak's signature and comes with Jobs' 1978 letter to Hatfield, creating an unusually direct connection between Apple's two founders and a single machine. Yet Jobs' letter is more than a piece of celebrity memorabilia. It shows what Apple wanted to happen to this particular computer.Apple had discontinued the Apple-1 in 1977 and began encouraging owners to trade their machines in for newer hardware. The company destroyed returned Apple-1 boards, helping reduce the surviving population to fewer than half of the 200 computers originally produced. Apple also had a practical reason for the push, since Wozniak was reportedly the only employee able to provide technical support for the ageing machine.Against that backdrop, Jobs' letter to Hatfield becomes something much more revealing than a founder's autograph. It is a surviving instruction to send one of those increasingly unwanted boards back to Apple.Why Hatfield turned down Apple's offerHatfield had contacted Apple because he was unhappy with the limited software available for the Apple-1. Jobs responded on January 18, 1978, signing as Apple's Vice President, Operations, and authorising Hatfield to return his Apple-1 without its memory chips along with a $400 check in exchange for an Apple II 4K board.Hatfield could keep the memory chips, but the computer itself was supposed to go back to Apple. The Apple II 4K board retailed for $598 at the time, making Jobs' offer a substantial concession. However, Hatfield decided the upgrade wasn't worth the additional $400 and kept his Apple-1 instead.A refusal that set up decades of valueThat refusal eventually became the defining moment in the computer's history. Hatfield packed the machine securely and carried it through multiple moves rather than discarding it when the Apple-1 became obsolete.He eventually sold it in 2013 for $40,000 when it was not functioning; it was later restored and demonstrated in working order. The computer was then sold at auction for $671,400, showing how dramatically the market had come to value surviving examples of Apple's first computer. It is now returning to the auction block with a potential price of $800,000.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.
